papers.title: Analytical Modeling of Thermal Shield-Induced Tilt Noise in Lunar Regolith: Constraints on Future Lunar Seismometers and Gravitational waves Detectors
papers.micro: The analytical framework provides a computationally efficient way to evaluate thermal-shield geometry, albedo contrast, and instrument placement for future lunar seismic and inertial gravitational-wave sensor deployments.
papers.abstract: Surface features such as thermal shields, insulating blankets, and exposed rocks modify the absorption of solar radiation in the lunar regolith, producing lateral temperature gradients missed by one-dimensional thermal models. These gradients cause thermoelastic deformation that tilts surface-deployed seismic instruments, adding long-period noise. We develop an analytical framework, based on Hankel transforms in a semi-infinite regolith, that treats these features as perturbations to a laterally uniform diurnal thermal state; linearity allows multiple features to be superposed. The framework is applied to the Apollo 14 Passive Seismic Experiment, including the seismometer thermal shield and surrounding instruments. The Apollo shield is a multilayer insulation (MLI) blanket that passes a fraction of the solar-flux fluctuation to the ground. Near local noon the shadow of the instrument body shifts by 2-5 cm across this dimly lit ground. This asymmetry dominates the tilt; its median amplitude spectral density reaches 7-8 x 10^(-11) rad/sqrt(Hz) in the 1-5 mHz band, about three orders of magnitude above that of an opaque shield. Enlarging an opaque shield lowers the tilt, but the body-shadow tilt of an MLI shield does not decrease with shield radius. Thermal heterogeneity can thus generate a tilt bias, present even during seismically quiet intervals, that should be included in the noise budget of future lunar horizontal seismometers and inertial GW accelerometers, and the optical transmission of the shield and the instrument's own shadow can matter more than shield size. The analytical framework provides a computationally efficient way to evaluate thermal-shield geometry, albedo contrast, and instrument placement for future lunar seismic and inertial gravitational-wave sensor deployments.

papers.title: An ALMA Survey of Molecular Gas in the Host Galaxies of Fast Radio Bursts
papers.micro: We present ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission and millimeter continuum measurements for 9 localized fast radio burst (FRB) hosts at z=0.05-0.38.
papers.abstract: We present ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission and millimeter continuum measurements for 9 localized fast radio burst (FRB) hosts at z=0.05-0.38. CO emission is significantly detected in 6 hosts and tentatively detected in one, yielding molecular gas masses of 2.2x10^8-1.0x10^10 Mo for a Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor. All 6 detections show spatially resolved emission and large-scale velocity gradients, several consistent with ordered disk rotation. FRB positions do not necessarily coincide with the brightest CO emission, and no distinct kinematic component is identified at the burst positions at the present kpc-scale resolution. Together with published data, we assemble the largest FRB-host sample with CO measurements or upper limits to date. CO-detected hosts tend to have larger molecular gas reservoirs and longer depletion times than stellar-mass- and star-formation-rate-matched xCOLD GASS galaxies. They also tend to have higher molecular gas fractions and longer depletion times than expected from molecular-gas scaling relations. However, survival analyses including non-detections do not establish a significant difference in molecular gas mass or gas fraction. Both hosts detected in CO and HI have molecular-to-atomic mass ratios within the broad scatter of comparison galaxies. Our results highlight diverse cold-gas environments rather than a uniformly molecular-gas-rich FRB host population. At the position of the repeating FRB20201124A, the measured 98 GHz continuum flux density is above the predicted star-formation contribution and lies at the lower end of or below an extrapolation of the VLA spectrum. These results allow a compact persistent-source contribution and a possible spectral turnover between centimeter and millimeter wavelengths, although the present sensitivity and resolution prevent a firm separation from surrounding star-forming emission.

papers.title: Detection of GRB 261010A with GRID-11B
papers.micro: At both candidate host redshifts (z=0.070 and 0.785), the low ε values and their positions relative to the Amati relation suggest Type-I-like properties.
papers.abstract: We report GRID-11B observations of the main emission episode of GRB 261010A. We measure T₉₀=5.68^+1.04_−0.32 s and a minimum variability timescale of 51.6^+10.5_−9.8 ms. Its spectrum is described by a cutoff power law with Ep=1089⁺¹⁷¹₋₈₀ keV. At both candidate host redshifts (z=0.070 and 0.785), the low ε values and their positions relative to the Amati relation suggest Type-I-like properties. These properties, despite the long duration, resemble those of GRB 211211A and motivate investigation of a possible compact-object merger origin.

papers.title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
papers.micro: Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.
papers.abstract: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf (d=23.8 pc), around which a 13.4586^+0.0044_−0.0067 d planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range 2−100 d by at most Δln Z=−0.4 for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.

papers.title: PLATON 7: An ultra-fast exoplanet atmospheric retrieval code
papers.micro: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018.
papers.abstract: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018. We introduce PLATON 7, a complete rewrite of PLATON using Claude Fable 5. The biggest changes are that PLATON now uses JAX for all intensive calculations, and these calculations are now performed in single precision instead of double precision. These two changes speed up the code by a factor of  60 with negligible decrease in accuracy, allowing it to compute a 0.8–5.3 um transmission spectrum at R=20k in 0.35 ms on a RTX 5090. We also introduce several new features, including support for two-limb retrievals, patchy clouds, and more opacities (particularly OCS and CS2). PLATON is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ideasrule/platon.

papers.title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
papers.micro: Individual SMBHB signals can significantly skew the recovery of the GWB amplitude and spectral index.
papers.abstract: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. In this work, we analyze how the presence of this signal could affect our detection statistics for the GWB, and how the presence of the GWB can affect our search for the SMBHB system. We find that individual SMBHB signals can significantly skew the recovery of the GWB amplitude and spectral index. However, when the SMBHB signals are recovered consistently, we are again able to recover the GWB power-law parameters, highlighting the importance of joint searches in future PTA searches for GWs. We also explore the rate of improvement of parameter estimation uncertainty, giving insight to the types of signals most likely to be identified well enough to enable multimessenger analyses.

papers.title: Blazars through the eyes of REDSoX and GOSoX
papers.micro: REDSoX and GOSoX will be the first (and currently only) X-ray polarimeters capable of performing observations below 1 keV, opening a new observational window into high-energy polarimetry.
papers.abstract: Blazar polarimetric properties provide key constraints on the physical conditions within relativistic jets, offering insights into particle acceleration mechanisms, high-energy radiation processes, and jet composition. The Rocket Experiment Demonstration of a Soft X-ray Polarimeter (REDSoX) will serve as a precursor to the Globe Orbiting Soft X-ray Polarimeter (GOSoX), a state-of-the-art polarimeter designed for observations in the soft X-ray range (0.2-0.4 keV), with a planned launch for 2030. REDSoX and GOSoX will be the first (and currently only) X-ray polarimeters capable of performing observations below 1 keV, opening a new observational window into high-energy polarimetry. In this work, we investigate the soft X-ray polarimetric properties of blazars expected in the REDSoX and GOSoX band and assess the detectability of different samples of sources: one drawn from the RoboPol Monitoring Program, a statistically complete sample of gamma-ray-selected blazars spanning the low-, intermediate-, and high-synchrotron-peaked sources, and one cross-matched between the CAZ (CRTS, ATLAS, and ZTF) and eROSITA catalogs. We estimated the expected source fluxes in the selected energy bands through spectral energy distribution fitting performed with the Bjet-MCMC tool. We investigated the expected polarimetric properties under three competing emission scenarios: leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid, each one predicting distinct observational signatures. We assessed the detectability of every source by comparing our polarization degree predictions with the instrument's minimum detectable polarization function (MDP). Finally, we computed the detection probability for each source. This work offers a set of promising blazar targets for future observations with GOSoX, highlighting the mission's potential for probing relativistic jet physics through soft X-ray polarimetry.

papers.title: Water-ice formation in Ophiuchus follows the local irradiation
papers.micro: Photometric ice maps resolve this variation across entire clouds, and the SPHEREx and JWST ice surveys can test it spectroscopically.
papers.abstract: Water ice only appears on interstellar dust grains beyond a certain depth into a molecular cloud. This depth has so far been quoted as one extinction threshold per cloud. We measured the threshold along 43009 sightlines through the Ophiuchus cloud with the ice color-excess method, which converts archival WISE and Spitzer photometry of background stars into the peak optical depth of the 3 μm water-ice band. We sorted the sightlines by the 12 μm surface brightness of the cloud at fixed extinction, a proxy for the ultraviolet field that excites the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons at the cloud surface. The onset of ice formation lies at higher extinction toward sightlines with brighter 12 μm emission, ranging from AKSᵗʰ = 0.67 to 1.15 mag. It increases by 0.58 to 0.90 mag in AKS per factor of ten in 12 μm brightness, depending on the adopted reddening coefficient. Because the 12 μm-bright and -faint sightlines lie in different parts of the cloud, we repeated the comparison within each of the five subregions, and four of the subregions show the same trend. The trend also persists among sightlines with a similar amount of diffuse material around them. A later onset in more strongly irradiated gas is expected from photodesorption by external ultraviolet light, although a comparison of its size with models requires a calibration of the 12 μm brightness against the strength of the field. The extinction at which water ice appears thus varies with the local environment, which complicates comparisons between clouds. Photometric ice maps resolve this variation across entire clouds, and the SPHEREx and JWST ice surveys can test it spectroscopically.

papers.title: Charge Exchange Illuminates Turbulent Cold-Hot Interfaces
papers.micro: The system-wide CX-to-thermal soft X-ray ratio also depends on the volume-to-interface scale V/Aint, making CX a potential probe of multiphase structure in the CGM, galactic winds, and the GC.
papers.abstract: Cold-hot interfaces are ubiquitous in the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM), galactic winds, and the Galactic Center (GC), yet their microscopic contact regions are difficult to observe. Charge exchange (CX), in which a highly ionized metal ion captures an electron from a neutral donor and emits soft X-ray lines, directly probes these interfaces. We develop a subgrid CX model coupled to a nonequilibrium ionization (NEI) network in hydrodynamic simulations of radiative turbulent mixing layers. CX soft X-rays are confined to a thin, highly corrugated cold-hot interface (corrugation factor ∼10), whereas thermal emission fills the hot phase. Turbulent transport sustains high-charge ions at T∼ 10⁴-10⁵ K, where they encounter neutral donors. The low-temperature O VIII fraction exceeds that in a uniformly cooling isobaric parcel, demonstrating the importance of mixing to the ionization history. CX depletes this cool ion population, while continued entrainment maintains the supply. Including a metagalactic ionizing background changes the ion distribution and enhances CX surface brightness by a factor of a few in our CGM comparison, but preserves the cool origin of most CX emission. In the limit of sufficient neutral column, CX surface brightness is ion-supply limited: higher donor density increases local emissivity but shortens the reaction layer. The system-wide CX-to-thermal soft X-ray ratio also depends on the volume-to-interface scale V/Aint, making CX a potential probe of multiphase structure in the CGM, galactic winds, and the GC.

papers.title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopy Reveals Declining Abundance but a Non-Evolving Luminosity Function Shape
papers.micro: With spectroscopic follow-up from Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE on 24 candidates, we identify a sample of four LRDs with broad Hα emission.
papers.abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are an extremely abundant population of red, compact, broad-line objects primarily found in the early universe. At 5<z<8, they are at least 10 times more abundant than UV-selected quasars. Yet, how this population evolves towards lower redshift is unclear. In this work, we present our search for LRDs at cosmic noon (2≲ z≲ 4) in nearly 20 deg² of the Deep/UltraDeep fields of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP). Combining multiwavelength wide-field imaging surveys from 0.3 to 4.5 μm, we identify 266 photometric LRD candidates. With spectroscopic follow-up from Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE on 24 candidates, we identify a sample of four LRDs with broad Hα emission. With the purity of the photometric sample calibrated by spectroscopy, we estimate the number density of LRDs to be approximately 6.8×10⁻⁷ cMpc⁻³ at 2.10<z<2.55—this is nearly a factor of 35 decrease from their flat number density evolution at 4≲ z≲8 estimated from JWST spectroscopic surveys. The knee of the LRD optical luminosity function also remains consistently at M₅₅₀₀≈−22 mag across 2<z<5, below that of quasars. We further speculate that only the abundance of LRDs, but not the shape of their optical luminosity function, evolves with redshift, and the Roman Space Telescope will be able to test this decisively with a substantially larger sample of low-redshift LRDs.

papers.title: The MURALES survey. IX. MUSE observations and results for 3C radio sources at 0.3 < z < 0.82
papers.micro: The more extended EELRs usually have elongated morphologies and show well-ordered rotation.
papers.abstract: This is the ninth paper in the MUse RAdio Loud Emission lines Snapshot (MURALES) project series, presenting the results of observations of 3C radio sources obtained with the VLT/MUSE integral field spectrograph. Here, we investigate the morphology and kinematics of the extended emission line regions (EELRs) of 26 radio galaxies at intermediate redshift 0.3 < z < 0.82 and their relation with the radio ejecta. EELRs are observed in all but 4 of the 26 sources extending as far as 160 kpc from the host galaxy. They show different morphologies and kinematics usually related with the radio properties. The five sources associated with the smaller radio sources show highly disturbed gas kinematics. Several EELRs have a filamentary morphology, often forming bubbles inflated by the radio lobes. The more extended EELRs usually have elongated morphologies and show well-ordered rotation. We then confirm the general results obtained from the study of the source at lower redshift: radio galaxies are surrounded by super-disks, that is, structures of ionized gas on scales of many tens of kiloparsec, whose properties depend on a combination of the evolutionary state of the radio source and its orientation with respect to the super-disks.

papers.title: From Binary Wind to Radio Burst: Dispersion-Measure Evolution after Accretion-induced Collapse
papers.micro: The observed distribution of secular DM variation slope amplitudes and signs will be important for distinguishing among different models of DM variations in repeating FRBs.
papers.abstract: Secular changes in the dispersion measures (DMs) of repeating fast radio bursts probe the source-local plasma. Such DM time variability has been interpreted with spherical, single-density-profile models. Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of a white dwarf may instead follow binary interaction and occur inside a finite, anisotropic circumstellar structure. Here, we construct an angle-dependent toy model of aspherical AIC ejecta propagating through a pre-AIC free wind, shocked-wind bubble, swept-up external shell, and polar cavity, exploring a diffuse environment (number density of 1 cm⁻³, located at 10 pc) and a compact cloud (number density of 500 cm⁻³, located at 0.3 pc), bracketing ionized and initially neutral upstream gas. The unshocked ejecta initially yield DM∝ t⁻², while crossings of the finite wind-bubble interfaces produce breaks and curvature in DM(t). In initially neutral models, shock ionization can overcome geometric dilution: the total DM reverses from decline to growth after approximately 10–20 yr and later turns over as the finite reservoir is processed. Ionized-upstream models instead generally decline or flatten. Without fitting individual sources, our models span both signs and the approximate magnitudes of the secular DM-variation rates measured among repeaters. In this dynamical framework, DM evolution is set by shock propagation through the circumsource density and ionization structure, rather than the contemporaneous burst rate, distinguishing it from photoionization-driven scenarios. Consequently, in our model, an instantaneous (d DM/dt) is not a unique indicator of source age. We suggest that the observed distribution of secular DM variation slope amplitudes and signs will be important for distinguishing among different models of DM variations in repeating FRBs.

papers.title: Machine learning reveals new Galactic C-rich and O-rich AGB sources
papers.micro: We present a machine-learning (ML) classification of Galactic AGB candidates using Gaia DR3, identifying 304,090 O-rich and 4,227 C-rich sources.
papers.abstract: Identification of carbon-rich (C-rich) and oxygen-rich (O-rich) Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars is crucial to understanding the structure and dust sources of the Milky Way. We present a machine-learning (ML) classification of Galactic AGB candidates using Gaia DR3, identifying 304,090 O-rich and 4,227 C-rich sources. Our two-step approach, which involves similarity-based selection, followed by XGBoost classification that combines colour and spectroscopic features, demonstrates that a small, but high-quality training sample is sufficient for accurate identification even in massive datasets such as  140 million sources from Gaia DR3. The ML-identified stars occupy distinct regions in colour-magnitude and Gaia-2MASS diagrams, and comparison with stellar isochrones combined with Gaia distances allows estimates of their masses and ages. Spatial distributions show that O-rich AGB stars dominate the inner Galaxy, while C-rich AGB stars are concentrated toward the anti-Galactic centre. Vertical profiles indicate that massive O-rich (5-8 M☉) stars remain near the Galactic mid-plane, whereas C-rich (2.3-2.5 M☉) and low-mass O-rich (1-1.5 M☉) AGB stars are more vertically extended, with scale heights that increase with decreasing stellar mass and increasing stellar ages. C-rich AGB stars trace the Galactic warp at intermediate ages (1 Gyr), with warp amplitudes appearing larger than those traced by Cepheids. Intermediate-mass O-rich AGB stars ( 300 Myr) show tentative correspondence with several spiral arm features, while the C-rich distribution is too smooth for reliable identification with the current sample. These results highlight AGB stars as powerful probes of stellar evolution and Galactic dynamical processes.

papers.title: Effects of Preionisation in Radiative Shocks IV. A Spectral Grid Library of fully Radiative Shock Models with Time–Dependent Precursor
papers.micro: We present an extensive set of shock models calculated using an improved version of the MAPPINGS shock and photoionization code.
papers.abstract: Here we present an extensive set of shock models calculated using an improved version of the MAPPINGS shock and photoionization code. The new version of MAPPINGS, namely MAPPINGS V, has a greatly improved treatment of the precursor emission, a more robust adaptive-mesh shock solver (Sutherland & Dopita 2017), and new atomic data compared to MAPPINGS III, which was used by Allen et al. (2008) to create their widely used shock model grid. The new shock model library covers the shock velocity range 50-1000 km/s, and a wide range of initial conditions and updated abundances. We highlight how the newer models compare to the earlier grid, and discuss where the shock models are most likely to approximate conditions for various types of astrophysical objects. The emission that one expects to observe depends on a variety of factors, including the velocity of the shock, the density and abundance of material the shock is encountering, the magnetic field and the effective age of the shock.

papers.title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopic Identification and Broad-Line Properties
papers.micro: We present Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE spectroscopic follow-up observations of photometrically selected Little Red Dot (LRD) candidates targeting Hα at 2<z<3.
papers.abstract: We present Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE spectroscopic follow-up observations of photometrically selected Little Red Dot (LRD) candidates targeting Hα at 2<z<3. The apparent decline of LRDs at cosmic noon raises the question whether they retain the spectra of the high-redshift population. From a parent sample of 266 unresolved sources with V-shaped broadband SEDs, identified in 19.9 deg² of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program Deep/UltraDeep fields, we observe 24 and confirm broad Hα in 6. The remaining 18 candidates show no broad Hα. Four have Lyα redshifts, which place Hα outside our coverage for two. The other 14 have only photometric redshifts, so their Hα coverage is uncertain; they may have incorrect photometric redshifts, broad Hα fainter than LHα≈3×10⁴² erg s⁻¹, or not be LRDs. All six broad Hα lines are best fit by exponential profiles, with FWHM ≈ 950–2150 km s⁻¹. Three show Balmer absorption, all show Balmer decrements above Case B (Hα/Hβ≈ 8–34, though Hβ is not detected), and four have V-shaped SEDs consistent with JWST-selected LRD samples. Archival JWST/NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec spectroscopy independently confirm one source as an LRD. One of the six is X-ray detected at a luminosity typical of ordinary AGN and is better described as a broad-line AGN. Only one of seven dust-reddened F2M quasars and two of 38 heavily reddened quasars at 2<z<3 meet typical JWST V-shape criteria. Four of the six sources with broad Hα (67%) resemble JWST-selected LRDs, showing that ground-based photometric selection and spectroscopy can identify LRDs.

papers.title: Generative Bayesian modelling of radio antenna beams An application to the MeerKAT radio telescope
papers.micro: The 150 kB per-antenna footprint enables memory-slim integration into calibration and imaging software at negligible cost…
papers.abstract: Accurate primary beam models are essential for high-fidelity calibration and imaging in radio astronomy. Traditional approaches either lack the ability to represent realistic antenna patterns (analytical models) or become computationally prohibitive to interpolate for wide-bandwidth observations (electromagnetic simulations, direct holographic measurements). We develop a generative beam model that represents both the spatial structure and the frequency variations in the primary beam while remaining tractable for integration into calibration and imaging pipelines, achieving superior accuracy compared to existing parametric models and reducing data storage compared to data-based models. We adopt a non-parametric Bayesian framework grounded in information field theory, implemented using the NIFTy library. The model represents the beam as a base pattern subject to frequency-dependent geometric transformations (scaling and shifting). Performance is validated through posterior predictive checks (chi^2/dof   1) and compared against traditional models (Gaussian, Airy disc, JimBeam, Eidos, electromagnetic simulation). We apply the method to holographic data of the array-averaged MeerKAT Stokes I beam in the L band. The model achieves 400:1 data compression while preserving statistical consistency with holographic measurements, and outperforms existing approaches by more than an order of magnitude in mean squared deviation. Zernike decomposition of the base beam, combined with the geometric transformations, enables efficient beam reconstruction at arbitrary spatial resolution. The 150 kB per-antenna footprint enables memory-slim integration into calibration and imaging software at negligible cost, scales favourably to large arrays and wide bandwidths, and can be readily adapted to other radio telescopes.

papers.title: Modeling Asymmetries in Be Star Disks Using Spectro-interferometric H-alpha Observations from the CHARA Array's VEGA Instrument
papers.micro: The differential interferometric visibility amplitudes and phases across the Hα emission line reveal clues about the asymmetries present in their disks.
papers.abstract: Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars with outflowing decretion disks. The observational record shows that in many cases the peaks of their Hα flux profile vary on long timescales. These changes are probably caused by the development of disk brightness asymmetries that are related to global disk oscillation modes. Here we present spectro-interferometric observations made with the CHARA Array interferometer and the VEGA beam combiner that document the interferometric data across the Hα line for the Be stars γ Cas, φ Per, ζ Tau, and β CMi. The differential interferometric visibility amplitudes and phases across the Hα emission line reveal clues about the asymmetries present in their disks. Here we describe a model of the Hα formation that calculates the emission intensity at spatial positions around the star and disk. The parameters describing the disk and the oscillation mode are optimized to match the interferometric data and contemporaneous Hα spectroscopy. The analysis confirms the presence of strong disk asymmetries at the time of the observations (2020) in the cases of γ Cas and φ Per, and hints that weaker oscillation modes were also present in the disks of ζ Tau and β CMi. The success of this single epoch study demonstrates the promise of future interferometric programs to investigate how the modes precess within the disk and grow and decline over time.

papers.title: NGC 1300: A rich reservoir of ultraluminous X-ray sources
papers.micro: Within the optical extent of the galaxy, we identify 42 X-ray sources, including six ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) and 13 ULX candidates.
papers.abstract: We present the first systematic multi-epoch study of the X-ray source population of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1300, using 12 archival Chandra observations spanning more than 15 years and archival Swift/XRT monitoring. Within the optical extent of the galaxy, we identify 42 X-ray sources, including six ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) and 13 ULX candidates. The candidates have measured luminosities below 10³⁹ erg s⁻¹, but their upper uncertainty bounds reach or exceed this threshold in at least one epoch. We examine source luminosities, long-term variability, broad-band spectral properties, and epoch-resolved X-ray luminosity functions (XLFs). Ten sources meet our transient criterion, seven have a variability significance of Svar≥3, and four meet both criteria. X32 is a highly variable ULX with a peak X-ray luminosity of 1.5×10⁴⁰ erg s⁻¹, more than 715 times the non-detection upper limit. The hardness-intensity diagrams show diverse spectral behavior among the luminous sources, with no common hardness-luminosity evolution. X32 remains predominantly hard despite its large luminosity variations, and its X-ray colors are consistent with the empirical high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) region of the color-color diagram. The cumulative XLFs above 10³⁸ erg s⁻¹ have slopes of β≃0.6 to 1.0, with evidence for a broken power law in only a few epochs. The number of off-nuclear sources reaching 10³⁹ erg s⁻¹ ranges from zero to four per epoch. Long-term source variability thus strongly shapes the bright end of the XLF and makes the observed ULX census of NGC 1300 strongly epoch dependent. Multi-epoch monitoring is essential for establishing representative ULX populations in nearby galaxies.

papers.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia IV. New planetary-mass companions found in debris disks
papers.micro: When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties.
papers.abstract: When spatially resolved, debris disks often exhibit structures (gaps, rings, and spirals) that may indicate the presence of unseen planetary-mass companions. However, such planets have not been detected in most cases. Gaia opens a new mass-separation parameter space for detecting unseen planets. A tool named GaiaPMEX has been developed to detect and characterize companions to stars. It is based on two binarity indicators derived from DR3: the Gaia astrometric signature and, when the sources were also observed by Hipparcos, the Gaia-Hipparcos proper motion anomaly. We used GaiaPMEX on 94 stars hosting resolved debris disks to search for companions. When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties. We found stellar or substellar companions around five targets (HD 54341, HD 146897, HD 206893, HD 107146, and HD 106906) and indications (2 sigma) for companions around three additional targets (BD+45 598, TWA 7, and HD 120326). The companion to the 150 Myr star HD 107146, which harbors a ring-like dust disk, is found to be a 2-6 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting between 2-10 au. A massive 3-20 Jupiter-mass companion is found 3-10 au from the close binary HD 106906, which already hosts a remote planet orbiting at more than 700 au, and an edge-on disk. The tentative companions to TWA 7 and HD 120326 are planetary-mass companions at 1-3 au. Both stars host a multiple-ring system. We finally provide meaningful upper limits on the possible presence of companions in the range of 0-100 au around a few emblematic stars (49 Cet, AU Mic, beta Pic, and epsilon Eri) and stars hosting well-defined ring-like structures.

papers.title: SciPIC-lite: A flexible Halo Occupation Distribution pipeline aimed at clustering observables
papers.micro: We present SciPIC-lite, a new public Python library for fast…
papers.abstract: The Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) framework provides a flexible approach to modelling the galaxy–halo connection in cosmological simulations, encoding the statistical relationship between galaxies and their host dark matter haloes. We present SciPIC-lite, a new public Python library for fast, flexible, and user-friendly HOD modelling, designed to populate dark matter haloes extracted from cosmological simulations with galaxies and to provide a comprehensive suite of tools for their subsequent analysis. The library is built around a modular and extensible codebase that incorporates the full breadth of the HOD framework, from the core occupation functions to a wide range of physically motivated extensions, making it suitable for a broad spectrum of galaxy clustering applications. We validate and characterise the performance of SciPIC-lite by developing a pipeline to fit the two-point correlation functions of Hα-selected galaxies from the Flagship 2 simulation across multiple redshift bins. To this end, we populate AbacusSummit dark matter haloes with galaxies according to a variety of HOD parametrisations. We assess the robustness of the fits with respect to the choice of HOD parametrisation and the inclusion of physically motivated extensions, including assembly bias, velocity bias, conformity, and halo profile rescaling. The best-fit models are found to be remarkably robust across different HOD parametrisations and fitting configurations, with reduced χ² values clustering tightly around a common value regardless of the model adopted. We exploit these results to generate new AbacusSummit-based galaxy mocks that accurately reproduce the clustering properties of the Flagship 2 Hα galaxy population.

papers.title: The Effect of Dust Grain Growth and Stellar Metallicity on Gas Giant Planet Formation by Disk Instability
papers.micro: Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.
papers.abstract: The formation of gas giant planets by the gas disk gravitational instability (GDGI) mechanism depends sensitively on the thermodynamics of the protoplanetary disk gas: disk gas must be able to cool on orbital timescales for dense clumps to become gravitationally unstable and contract to form protoplanets. Since disk cooling is regulated by the opacity of the dust grains embedded in the gas, the properties of these dust grains are critical for the GDGI mechanism. Grain growth to larger sizes than assumed in traditional opacity models for solar metallicity, as well as protostars with sub-solar metallicity, should have lower opacity disks that are more conducive to planet formation by GDGI. Here we use a three dimensional radiative hydrodynamics and gravitation code to compute the evolution of the GDGI in 0.091 M☉ disks with varied initial minimum values (1.3 to 2.7) of the Toomre criterion orbiting solar-mass protostars. Three sets of eight models are computed: one with the standard opacity, and two more with the opacity reduced by arbitrary factors of 10 or 100. As expected, the reduced opacity models result in enhanced disk fragmentation by the GDGI and the production of more self-gravitating clumps than the standard opacity models. Nevertheless, all three opacities form similar self-gravitating clumps at this early phase of clump evolution, with masses of 0.2 to 0.7 MJup and semimajor axes between 6 and 13 au. Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.

papers.title: Dynamical friction on an extended satellite revisited
papers.micro: We find that, at fixed galaxy model and satellite mass, the more extended the satellite, the weaker is the effect of DF.
papers.abstract: The original formulation of Chandrasekhar dynamical friction (DF) was developed for a point-like particle moving in a infinite and homogeneous medium. However, despite very useful order of magnitude estimates of the slowing-down time scales of a test mass in more realistic finite-sized models, high resolution N−body simulations often hint at a breakdown of Chandrasekhar's formalism (typically overestimating the effect of DF) for massive satellites sinking in the host galaxy. More advanced semi-analytical treatment of the DF expression managed to partially reduce said discrepancy, even though an accurate comparison with numerical simulations still remains difficult, specifically due to the interplay between the DF force and the tidal stress effects on an extended stellar systems sinking in the gravitational potential of the parent galaxy or halo. In this study we perform ad hoc N−body simulations of a satellite orbiting in a simple spherical galaxy model, for different values of the initial orbital eccentricity, satellite mass, scale radius and velocity anisotropy profile of the host model. We adopt an N−body code where the self-consistent interaction among the particles representing the galaxy can be substituted by the effect of the static smooth potential of the system's continuum limit. Moreover, the satellite itself is either modeled with Nsat particles or represented by a single particle with an effective size parametrized in the form of the force exchanged with the other simulation particles representing the galaxy. We find that, at fixed galaxy model and satellite mass, the more extended the satellite, the weaker is the effect of DF. This trend, which is found for both isotropic and radially anisotropic host systems, is particularly evident for orbits with initial orbital eccentricity exceeding ≈0.3.

papers.title: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich Velocity Reconstruction Using Vision Transformers
papers.micro: Our approach can be applied to full-resolution maps from existing and near-term CMB and LSS datasets.
papers.abstract: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich (kSZ) velocity reconstruction uses correlations between maps of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and a tracer of large scale structure (LSS) to infer the large-scale peculiar velocity field. Standard approaches to kSZ velocity reconstruction use quadratic estimators that are Fisher optimal for purely Gaussian fields. Here, we develop a pipeline for kSZ velocity reconstruction based on Vision Transformers (ViT) and show that this approach can improve the fidelity of velocity reconstruction. This is consistent with the network utilizing non-Gaussian information in the inputs that the quadratic estimators do not, though with the single simulation realization we have access to, we cannot exclude overfitting. Our approach can be applied to full-resolution maps from existing and near-term CMB and LSS datasets.

papers.title: Information-Criterion-Driven, Non-linear Deprojection of Angular Imaging Systematics for the SPHEREx Galaxy Clustering Sample
papers.micro: We demonstrate these features on SPHEREx-like lognormal mock catalogues with injected contamination of various spatial profiles, amplitudes, and levels of complexity.
papers.abstract: Imaging systematics that inject false, or suppress true, galaxy clustering signals are of primary concern for current- and next-generation galaxy surveys, such as the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx) in its search for local primordial non-Gaussianity fNL. As statistical errors shrink with growing galaxy samples, systematic rather than statistical uncertainties come to dominate the cosmological error budget. For effects whose spatial patterns are known or well-modelled a priori, a common mitigation approach regresses (deprojects) the density variation associated with a known angular template. In this work we present and demonstrate novel aspects of this procedure as will be applied to the SPHEREx galaxy clustering sample. These include flexible – but, crucially, constrained and interpretable – non-linear basis regression with polynomial/spline bases, and aggressive information criterion-driven automated template selection with an associated unbiased two-stage regression, using agreement between two independent selectors as a consistency diagnostic. The method automatically selects a template set of minimal-but-sufficient complexity while limiting the number of templates actually regressed, minimising cosmological information loss and making modern additive-plus-multiplicative approaches tractable. We demonstrate these features on SPHEREx-like lognormal mock catalogues with injected contamination of various spatial profiles, amplitudes, and levels of complexity. Principled, signal-preserving deprojection of the kind demonstrated here is a crucial step towards achieving SPHEREx's goal of σ(fNL) < 0.5.

papers.title: Determining the Spin and Orbital Period of the Asynchronous Cataclysmic Variable X10 in 47 Tucanae
papers.micro: We find a white dwarf spin period of P_spin = 4.2683 h and derive an orbital period of Porb = 4.6779 h from the beat modulation.
papers.abstract: The X-ray source X10 in the globular cluster 47 Tuc has been identified as a cataclysmic variable (CV). With a suggested 4.7 hour periodicity, and a soft X-ray spectrum, it appears to be an unusually X-ray luminous (LX=2.2×10³² erg s⁻¹) polar CV. We use 286 ks of Chandra X-ray Observatory observations of 47 Tuc to study the X-ray timing behavior of 47 Tuc X10. X10 shows clear pulsations in the data, with occasional phase shifts. These suggest that X10 is an asynchronous polar CV, where the spin and orbital periods are slightly misaligned, and the dominant accretion flow shifts from one pole to the other. We use a Lomb-Scargle periodogram to suggest potential spin and orbital periods, then model the X-ray lightcurve using simple sinusoids to represent emission from each accretion pole, switching which pole is visible on the beat period. We find a white dwarf spin period of P_spin = 4.2683 h and derive an orbital period of Porb = 4.6779 h from the beat modulation. This large degree of asynchronism (8.8%) suggests that X10 is in an unstable equilibrium, and may be a transitional system between an intermediate polar and a fully synchronized polar.

papers.title: The role of gas on the collisional runaway path to supermassive black hole seeds
papers.micro: Our results show increases in BH mass of ∼ 8% for low gas fractions, to ∼ 44% at 20% gas fraction.
papers.abstract: The origin of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remains unclear, despite observational evidence for their rapid formation in the early Universe, as evidenced by active galactic nuclei (AGN) at high redshift. In this paper, we investigate stellar dynamics in dense, gas-embedded clusters. We explore how gas influences the runaway collision process and the subsequent formation of SMBH seeds in a global instability scenario. We perform a series of coupled N-body and SPH simulations using the AMUSE framework, with the stellar and gaseous components interacting gravitationally via the BRIDGE method. We use 12 initial condition models with equal-mass stars following Plummer distributions, with total masses ranging from 10³ to 5 × 10⁵ M☉, virial radii from 0.005 to 0.1 pc, and stellar masses of 1, 10 and 50 M☉. For each model, we perform four simulations with gas fractions ranging from 0% to 20%, resulting in a total of 48 simulations. The gas is sampled with the same spatial distribution as the stars, with a mass ratio per particle of mSPH/m = 0.01, where m is the stellar mass. We find that in most of our simulations, higher gas fractions lead to the formation of more massive black hole, as the core collapses earlier, triggering collisions through gas–star interactions. Our results show increases in BH mass of ∼ 8% for low gas fractions, to ∼ 44% at 20% gas fraction. The core collapse time is also shortened, with the strongest reduction at 20% gas fraction (∼ 27%). The transonic regime of our initial conditions is where dynamical friction is most efficient in principle. Although our simulations do not fully resolve this effect, gas–star interactions are the principal mechanism driving the enhancement in BH formation efficiency, in the absence of other dissipation mechanisms.

papers.title: Magnetic vector potentials and helicity in periodic domains
papers.micro: Periodic domains together with a mean magnetic flux lead to contradicting results about the value of the magnetic helicity and we show in a few thought experiments fundamental…
papers.abstract: For a magnetic field in three-dimensional Euclidean space, we argue about the existence of a magnetic vector potential in a finite cuboid with periodic boundary conditions. We first argue in physical terms by representing periodic domains as tori and show that in some cases, the generating electric current is unphysical. We then represent magnetic fields and vector potentials as differential 2 and 1-forms. For a given magnetic field we ask the question whether a corresponding vector potential exists. Singly periodic domains are shown to always allow for a vector potential. For doubly periodic domains it only exists if the net magnetic flux through the non-periodic dimension vanishes, while for triply periodic domains the net flux must vanish in all directions. This has implications for the definition of magnetic helicity in periodic domains. We show that periodic domains together with a mean magnetic flux lead to contradicting results about the value of the magnetic helicity and we show in a few thought experiments fundamental contradictions to the interpretation as the linking of magnetic field lines. For the helicity we can even construct magnetic fields in periodic domains for which the magnetic helicity exists, but the calculations of the magnetic helicity do not lead to meaningful results due to the gauge freedom. With that we conclude that in presence of a mean magnetic field the calculated magnetic helicity cannot be interpreted geometrically in a straightforward way. However, using the winding gauge we can recover the geometric interpretation of the helicity as the flux averaged magnetic field line winding. Finally, for the solar relevant non-periodic domain with finite point-wise flux and zero integrated flux, using an appropriate gauge transformation the magnetic helicity can be shown to vanish. The winding helicity, however, would lead to a non-vanishing value here.

papers.title: Broad-line ambiguity in IC 1495
papers.micro: The model-dependent 2024 broad-H-alpha candidate and limited 2004 sensitivity do not establish a change in broad-line visibility between the epochs.
papers.abstract: Published analyses disagree on whether the 2004 6dFGS spectrum of IC 1495, a barred Seyfert galaxy in the 2MIG isolated-galaxy catalogue, contains broad H-alpha. We compare it with a 2024 SDSS-V/BOSS spectrum to assess changes in broad-line visibility. In 2024, the [O III] profile favours a blueshifted wing with intrinsic FWHM  640 km/s, while [S II] and [O I] favour single-component fits. Among six H-alpha+[N II] models with free narrow-line kinematics, the BIC-preferred fit includes broad H-alpha with intrinsic FWHM  2000 km/s. However, adding broad H-alpha worsens the BIC when H-alpha and [N II] share two narrow kinematic components. Broad H-alpha is not detected in the 2004 spectrum under the adopted criterion. Injection-recovery simulations of a reference broad component (FWHM  1930 km/s; broad-to-narrow H-alpha flux ratio 0.82) yield recovery fractions of 27-35% in baseline simulations and 11-55% across the grid. At 1.5 times this flux ratio, baseline recovery rises to 42-55%. Aperture and flux-calibration uncertainties limit absolute line-flux comparisons. Narrow-line excitation, Chandra spectroscopy (intrinsic N_H  2.3 x 10^23 cm^-2 in the fiducial model), and long-term optical and mid-infrared variability support an absorbed, variable Seyfert nucleus. The model-dependent 2024 broad-H-alpha candidate and limited 2004 sensitivity do not establish a change in broad-line visibility between the epochs.

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stellar Extinction Map of M31 from PHAT and PHAST Photometry
papers.micro: The map has been publicly released through the NADC platform and is expected to serve as an important observational basis for extinction correction in subsequent astronomical observations and…
papers.abstract: High-resolution extinction maps of resolved external galaxies, such as M31, are crucial not only for accurately correcting dust extinction and reddening toward individual sources within the galaxy, but also for characterizing the distribution and evolution of interstellar dust in external galactic environments. We aim to construct a high-resolution and large-coverage stellar-traced extinction map of M31, based on multi-band photometric data from the HST PHAT and PHAST surveys. Using a stellar template library built from the PARSEC stellar evolution models and adopting the average extinction law of M31, we apply a matching method analogous to the SPar algorithm to derive A_V values for approximately 65 million stars. The extinction map is then generated using a HEALPix adaptive-resolution scheme. The resulting map covers approximately two-thirds of the star-forming disk of M31, with a maximum spatial resolution of 1.61 arcsec. The median extinction across the map is A_V = 1.24 mag. Comparison with previously published stellar- and dust-emission-based extinction maps shows broadly similar large-scale morphology, while differences remain in the extinction values. The extinction map further reveals fine-scale features such as inter-arm filaments, supernova-driven cavities, and spur-like structures. The map has been publicly released through the NADC platform and is expected to serve as an important observational basis for extinction correction in subsequent astronomical observations and for related M31 scientific studies.

papers.title: High-precision proper motions toward the Galactic bulge Baade's window from a decade of DECam observations
papers.micro: Since the LSST camera shares the same CCD technology as DECam, this work offers a valuable precursor for crowded-field astrometry in the Rubin era.
papers.abstract: A complete characterization of the Galactic bulge stellar populations could offer important clues on the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. However, most bulge fields are hampered by high stellar crowding, strong interstellar extinction, and by heavy contamination from foreground disk stars. We aim to derive proper motions (PMs) towards the Baade's window by using DECam observations, extending kinematic studies of the Galactic bulge below the turn-off to a much larger field of view. We combined three datasets observed with DECam in the r-band spanning a ∼ 10-year baseline. As a pilot study, we only analyzed the field covered by a single detector. We developed an astrometric calibration pipeline that corrects for the DECam tree-ring pattern and residual distortions, tying all positions to the Gaia DR3 reference frame, and used them to derive PMs. We isolated the bulge population through a strict cut in μ_ℓ^(*), refined with a Gaia DR3 parallax selection. We measured PMs for 48 239 stars in the pilot field, with a median uncertainty of 0.65 mas yr⁻¹ at r₀<18 mag. Our PMs agree closely with Gaia DR3, and reaches ∼1.5 magnitudes deeper than Gaia and a comparable depth to VIRAC2 in terms of relative completeness. We found velocity dispersions along Galactic longitude and latitude of σ_μ_ℓ^(*)=2.76±0.03 mas yr⁻¹ and σμb=2.49±0.02 mas yr⁻¹ for the Galactic bulge, consistent with HST studies. We estimated a foreground contamination of ∼14% before any kinematic selection. The cleaned color-magnitude diagram reaches below the main-sequence turnoff, and shows no evidence for a large population younger than ∼4-5 Gyr in this field. Moreover, since the LSST camera shares the same CCD technology as DECam, this work offers a valuable precursor for crowded-field astrometry in the Rubin era.

papers.title: Accretor Luminosity as Probe of Orbital Evolution and Magnetic Braking in AM CVn Binaries
papers.micro: We test and constrain various proposed magnetic braking formalisms, for the white dwarf, helium star, and evolved cataclysmic variable (CV) channels for AM CVn formation.
papers.abstract: AM CVn binaries are ultracompact systems with orbital periods Porb ≲ 70 min, where a white dwarf accretes from a He-rich semidegenerate donor. At short orbital periods (Porb ≲ 20 min), rapid accretion reheats the accretor. As the system widens and the mass transfer rate decreases, the accretor follows standard white dwarf cooling at longer orbital periods (Porb ≳ 30 min). The accretor cooling luminosity then acts as a powerful probe into the orbital evolution of the binary. Recent observations show that the accretor appears brighter (younger) at long orbital periods, compared to models where orbital angular momentum loss is solely set by gravitational wave emission. We show that additional angular momentum loss, which we ascribe to magnetic braking of the donor, can better reproduce observations of accretor luminosity. We test and constrain various proposed magnetic braking formalisms, for the white dwarf, helium star, and evolved cataclysmic variable (CV) channels for AM CVn formation. None of the magnetic braking formalisms in their original form can reproduce the observations, but the widely popular magnetic braking proposed by Rappaport et al. 1983 boosted by a factor ≈ 5, or the saturated magnetic braking proposed by Matt et al. 2015 boosted by a factor of ≈ 150, yields satisfactory results. We also find that the CARB formalism, recently applied to the evolved CV channel, is strongly in tension with observations of accretor luminosity. Our models motivate UV spectroscopy observations, and dedicated WD atmosphere models for AM CVn accretors.

papers.title: Computing the Wave: Bridging Gravitational Wave and High-Energy-Physics software (with modular ROOT extensions)
papers.micro: Building on the prototype presented at ACAT 2024, we report on the consolidation of that work into a single…
papers.abstract: High-Energy Physics (HEP) and Gravitational Wave (GW) astronomy pursue different scientific goals, yet they face strikingly similar computing challenges and can enrich one another through shared software. Building on the prototype presented at ACAT 2024, we report on the consolidation of that work into a single, modular extension of the CERN ROOT data-analysis framework, freely distributed under RIOPlus. The library is now organised as a set of optional, dynamically loadable extensions covering configuration and file-format parsing (including the Gravitational Wave Frame (GWF) format and HDF5), remote and federated data access (OSDF/Pelican, S3, Kafka) with token-based credentials, an enhanced dynamic-display manager, an advanced signal-processing layer built on the KFR library, and a complex-capable tensor layer backed by LibTorch with ONNX interoperability. We summarise the design of each extension, outline the intended application to transient-noise (glitch) detection and classification, and update the FFT performance benchmark comparing KFR with FFTW. We close with the end-to-end ROOT-centred workflow these extensions enable, its current status, and an outlook toward column-wise RNTuple storage.

papers.title: Precise Radii of Visual Binaries with Dynamical Masses: ξ Bootis & 70 Ophiuchi
papers.micro: Within this mass range, radius inflation appears to be associated with short-period binary star systems.
papers.abstract: A new orbital solution for ξ Bootis (GJ 566 AB, P=152 yrs) and the recently revised orbital solution for 70 Ophiuchi (GJ 702 AB, P=88 yrs) yield component masses precise to 0.4%. Their relatively wide separations (>0.4^(′′)) allow the components to be studied independently, making them ideal for testing the predictions of stellar evolutionary models. We use the six-telescope near-infrared MIRC-X and MYSTIC beam combiners at the CHARA Array to measure the angular diameters of all 4 stars. Combined with precise Gaia DR3 parallax values and bolometric fluxes, these interferometric measurements translate to stellar radii that are precise to <2.4% and effective temperatures precise to <1.7%. We compare the measured radii and temperatures to four stellar evolutionary models (Lyon, Dartmouth, PARSEC, MIST). Over the mass range 0.67 − 0.91 M☉, all models reproduce the observed properties within a few standard deviations, with no systematic offsets. The pairs are coeval and consistent with independent age estimates, further validating model predictions. With physical separations greater than 20 au, these pairs show no evidence of radius inflation, despite being spectroscopically classified as chromospherically active, and in the case of ξ Bootis, probable members of the adolescent age (∼ 0.4 Gyr) Ursa Majoris Moving Group. In contrast, a set of 21 short-period (P≲ 10 days) eclipsing binary stars with similar dynamical masses and metallicities are larger and often cooler than these same model predictions. Within this mass range, radius inflation appears to be associated with short-period binary star systems.

papers.title: Disentangling Disk and Broad-Line Region Continuum Emission in a Sample of Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.micro: Upcoming time-resolved spectra will enable more detailed modelling and tighter constraints on the disk and BLR.
papers.abstract: Recent continuum reverberation-mapping measurements of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) indicate that the inter-band time lags are significantly larger than those predicted by the light travel times across the standard thin model. In addition, the observed u-band excess suggests the presence of diffuse continuum (DC) radiation originating in the broad-line region (BLR). Spectroscopically, the Balmer and Paschen jumps in DC emission are unique indicators to quantify the contributions of the BLR to the observed continuum. Here, we study the DC contributions of 31 AGNs, whose spectra are obtained with the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and with X-shooter on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). In each spectrum, at least one of the Balmer and Paschen jumps is covered. For each object, we performed radiative transfer calculations using Cloudy within the Locally Optimally-emitting Clouds (LOC) model to construct source-specific DC spectral templates. We quantified the DC contribution by incorporating these templates as continuum components in spectral decomposition. The average ratio of the DC to total (i.e., disk+DC) continua is  33% just below the Balmer jump ( 3625 Å). The Balmer jump provides a stronger constraint on the DC component than the Paschen jump. Simulations based on mock spectra further demonstrate that an unsuitable template can introduce systematic, wavelength-dependent biases to the inferred DC fraction. Our results underscore the importance of employing appropriate DC templates in the spectral decomposition to infer the substantial DC contribution. Upcoming time-resolved spectra will enable more detailed modelling and tighter constraints on the disk and BLR.

papers.title: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
papers.micro: The EDE tail retains observable information about the underlying scalar potential that is not captured by the conventional peak parameters alone.
papers.abstract: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the EDE tail, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and α-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations. Confronting this framework with cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and supernova observations, we find an improved fit to the high-ℓ CMB data together with a higher inferred bestfit H₀. Our results show that the EDE tail retains observable information about the underlying scalar potential that is not captured by the conventional peak parameters alone. This provides a complementary route for constructing and observationally distinguishing EDE scenarios, and potentially for further alleviating the Hubble tension.

papers.title: Ultraviolet Observations of Solar Active Phenomena
papers.micro: Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopic observations provide information on the fractionation of different chemical elements, in particular those elements with low first ionization potential.
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet observations of the Sun have revolutionized our understanding of the structure and dynamics of the solar atmosphere. From the chromosphere all the way to the corona, there are ubiquitous jets due to magnetic reconnection and associated with type III radio bursts. Sporadic flares occur in the corona, representing an inevitable breakup of magnetic energy accumulation as new magnetic flux continues to pump into the solar atmosphere, which is further shuffled by solar surface motions. Once large-scale eruptions occur, magnetized plasmas are expelled out into the interplanetary space, leaving globally propagating waves and the following dimmings. The waves can be utilized to diagnose the coronal magnetic field which cannot be measured directly, and the dimmings can be used to estimate the ejected mass of eruptions and magnetic connectivity. Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopic observations provide information on the fractionation of different chemical elements, in particular those elements with low first ionization potential. Thanks to the high spatial resolution of solar observations, all these results are believed to shed light on our understanding of the activity on other stars which cannot be imaged.

papers.title: IGRINS-2 Reveals an Oxygen-rich Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-12 b: Resolving the C/O Controversy
papers.micro: We present high-resolution (R ∼ 45,000) near-infrared dayside emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b with IGRINS-2 on Gemini North during post-eclipse phases.
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown that measurements of hot-Jupiter atmospheric composition, including carbon-to-oxygen (C/O) and refractory-to-volatile (R/V) abundance ratios, provide powerful diagnostics of the chemistry and formation of gas giant planets. Important questions remain about the atmospheric composition of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b: its dayside C/O ratio remains under debate, and its R/V ratio is not yet well constrained. We present high-resolution (R ∼ 45,000) near-infrared dayside emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b with IGRINS-2 on Gemini North during post-eclipse phases. Cross-correlation analysis reveals volatile molecular signals of H₂O and CO together with tentative signals of OH and gas-phase refractories in the planetary atmosphere. The planetary signals appear in emission, indicating a thermal inversion in the dayside atmosphere. A chemically consistent Bayesian retrieval yields C/O =0.72^+0.08_−0.10, disfavoring carbon-rich dayside solutions with C/O >1 at greater than 5σ. This independent, line-resolved measurement supports an oxygen-rich atmosphere, providing a new constraint on the long-standing C/O controversy surrounding WASP-12 b. Our retrieval also yields a host-star-normalized R/V ratio, [R/V]*=0.17^+0.22_−0.23, which is consistent with those of other ultra-hot Jupiters similarly characterized with IGRINS/IGRINS-2. Although the sample remains small, this consistency suggests a shared atmospheric chemistry among these planets, potentially reflecting similar proportions of accreted volatile and refractory material.

papers.title: The relation between DCN/DNC ratios and gas temperature in late-stage massive star-forming regions using Yebes observations
papers.micro: These results suggest that [DCN]/[DNC] may be governed not only by HCN/HNC isomeric chemistry but also by temperature-dependent deuterium fractionation pathways and the chemical evolution of dense gas.
papers.abstract: Deuterated molecules probe the physical and chemical evolution of molecular clouds and star-forming regions. Their abundances depend on temperature, density, and evolutionary stage. DCN and DNC are relatively abundant deuterated isomers that probe temperature-dependent deuterium chemistry. Although [HCN]/[HNC] is often thought to increase in warmer gas, the temperature dependence of [DCN]/[DNC] remains less well constrained. To investigate how [DCN]/[DNC] depends on the gas kinetic temperature, we observed the J=1-0 transitions of DCN, DNC, H¹³CN, HN¹³C, HC¹⁵N, and H¹⁵NC toward 101 late-stage massive star-forming regions using the Yebes 40m telescope. Gas kinetic temperatures were estimated from CH₃CCH 5-4, whose rotation temperature is closely related to the kinetic temperature of dense gas. These temperatures were adopted in the column density calculations and in the analysis of temperature-dependent abundance ratios. We find a moderate positive correlation between the abundance ratio [DCN]/[DNC] and kinetic temperature, which is statistically significant and indicates that DCN becomes progressively more abundant relative to DNC in warmer gas. A weak negative correlation with temperature is observed for D_frac( HNC), whereas no statistically significant correlation is found for D_frac( HCN). The [HCN]/[HNC] ratios show substantial scatter and no statistically significant correlation with temperature, possibly due in part to optical-depth effects in the ¹³C isotopologues and the limited sensitivity of the ¹⁵N isotopologue observations. These results suggest that [DCN]/[DNC] may be governed not only by HCN/HNC isomeric chemistry but also by temperature-dependent deuterium fractionation pathways and the chemical evolution of dense gas.

papers.title: Fast and accurate large-volume Lyman-α forest mocks with three-dimensional U-Net trained on IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO
papers.micro: We present a field-level emulator, based on a three-dimensional U-Net, that maps approximate density and velocity fields directly to Lyα optical depth and transmitted flux.
papers.abstract: The Lyman-α forest probes matter structure at z≳2, constraining baryon acoustic oscillations, neutrino masses, and dark matter properties. Interpreting current and upcoming spectroscopic surveys requires mock catalogues spanning Gpc-scale volumes while capturing small-scale intergalactic medium physics. This combination of high resolution and large volume is prohibitively expensive for hydrodynamical simulations. We present a field-level emulator, based on a three-dimensional U-Net, that maps approximate density and velocity fields directly to Lyα optical depth and transmitted flux. At z∼3, we train in small volumes and test on much larger, independent ones in two settings: IllustrisTNG (training on a 110 cMpc box and testing on a 300 cMpc box with 2LPT and N-body inputs) and FLAMINGO (training on 1 cGpc and testing on 2.8 cGpc with N-body inputs). The hydrodynamical statistics of TNG and FLAMINGO differ appreciably over their common k-range, by ∼15% in P1D, ∼17% in the bispectrum, and ∼40% in the connected trispectrum, although their normalized power-spectrum correlation structures remain broadly similar. Within each suite, the emulator reproduces P1D to 2.8% in TNG and 5.6% in FLAMINGO, the bispectrum to 4–5%, and the trispectrum to 10–16%, while also recovering the flux PDF and broad correlation structure. Field-level emulation thus provides a practical route to large-volume Lyα-forest mocks for current and future surveys.

papers.title: Accurately Measuring Variability Properties from Noisy Light Curves
papers.micro: Our results establish statistical limits for SF measurements in the weak-variability regime and offer a framework for accurately measuring low-amplitude variability in AGNs (e.g.…
papers.abstract: Modern time-domain surveys probe optical variability near photometric error, challenging weak-signal recovery. The structure function (SF) is widely used for characterizing variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), but its statistical recovery limits are unclear. Using simulated light curves with realistic errors, we compare three SF estimators from the literature: two non-parametric (pairwise noise subtraction and Bayesian) and one parametric. All recover intrinsic SF when variability dominates, but diverge in the weak regime. The pairwise noise-subtraction estimator approaches an artificial floor when negative variance estimates are discarded, with the floor set by photometric precision and sampling rather than intrinsic variability. The parametric method suffers degeneracy, while the Bayesian estimator yields nearly unbiased SF estimates given well-calibrated photometric errors and adequate sampling. We also derive an idealized detection threshold linking intrinsic variability, photometric precision, and pair counts, providing a reference for assessing the detectability of weak signals. Our results establish statistical limits for SF measurements in the weak-variability regime and offer a framework for accurately measuring low-amplitude variability in AGNs (e.g., extremely stable quasars) and in new populations such as little red dots discovered by JWST.

papers.title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
papers.micro: Compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts.
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4–2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.

papers.title: Revisiting the Double Cluster in Perseus: Are NGC 869 and NGC 884 a true binary system?
papers.micro: These results indicate that the system is not currently gravitationally bound and does not constitute a binary cluster.
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive study of the Double Cluster in Perseus, NGC 869 and NGC 884, to investigate their nature and evolutionary state. By combining new CCD UBV(RI)KC photometry with high-precision astrometry and photometry from Gaia DR3, we determine robust astrophysical parameters, including colour excess, distance, and age. Our analysis confirms that both clusters are young, with an age of 12±1 Myr, and share similar photometric distances of 2.29 kpc. By integrating these observational constraints with completeness-corrected mass estimates and a suite of N-body simulations, we examine the kinematic and phase-space properties of the system. We find that the internal kinematics of NGC 884 exhibit a stronger and more coherent expansion signature than NGC 869. Our dynamical simulations demonstrate a rapid increase in the separation of the pair during the first 100 Myr, exceeding 1 kpc. These results indicate that the system is not currently gravitationally bound and does not constitute a binary cluster. Instead, the Double Cluster is presently unbound, and the forward integrations predict that its components will continue to diverge under the influence of their relative motion and the Galactic potential.

papers.title: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
papers.micro: We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data.
papers.abstract: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency ω≃ 51 and lowers χ² by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at ω≃ 31 and lowers χ² by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to Aosc < 0.056 and Aosc < 0.062 (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.

papers.title: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra
papers.micro: We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra…
papers.abstract: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.

papers.title: Characterising stellar photometry with invertible neural networks: Joint inference of stellar parameters and extinction
papers.micro: Only log(age/yr) has proven harder to constrain with an RMSE of 0.56 dex.
papers.abstract: We introduce an extension to a simulation-based deep-learning approach for the characterisation of stellar photometry and investigate the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar properties and extinction. We used the PARSEC stellar evolutionary models to train a conditional invertible neural network (cINN) to jointly estimate full posterior distributions of stellar parameters and extinction. We tested our cINN on synthetic data and real Gaia+2MASS photometry of the two star-forming regions Taurus and Upper Scorpius. We compared our predicted extinction maps to two independent catalogues based on Gaia XP-spectra. On synthetic test data, our trained cINN exhibited a good predictive performance, achieving root mean squared errors (RMSEs) for the maximum a posteriori point estimates of about 0.16 mag for AV, 0.07 dex for log(Teff/K), 0.16 dex for log(g/cms⁻²), 0.2 dex for log(L/L☉) and 0.1 dex for log(Mini/M☉). Only log(age/yr) has proven harder to constrain with an RMSE of 0.56 dex. On the Gaia+2MASS observations of Taurus and Upper Scorpius, we retrieved reasonable extinction maps, exhibiting structures that are visually consistent with local clouds. Compared to the independent XP-spectra-based extinction studies, we found a good qualitative agreement and recovered the same prominent spatial structures. Quantitatively, however, we identified an average systematic overestimation of extinction in our approach of 0.5-0.7 mag compared to the spectroscopic studies. We investigated these offsets and identified photometric and distance uncertainties, which are currently unaccounted for in our approach, as likely causes. In conclusion, we demonstrated the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar parameters and extinction with our cINN approach, making it a promising avenue to further pursue for robust and efficient analysis of large photometric surveys.
